name: Jet Freight Logistics Ltd
title: Jet Freight Logistics Ltd - 543420 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Asset-light air freight forwarder with no supply discipline metrics; H1 FY27 revenue ~Rs 297 Cr, PAT margin ~1.5%, and management guides FY27 revenue Rs 580-600 Cr with no capacity or utilisation data.

summary.headline: Jet Freight H1 FY27 revenue about ₹297 Cr, with PAT margin near 1.5% and management guiding FY27 revenue to ₹580–600 Cr.
summary.overview: Management presented H1 FY27 (six months to 30 September 2026) revenue of about ₹297 Cr, with EBITDA margin of about 4.58% and PAT margin of about 1.52% (CFO also cited 1.55%). Shipments rose from 430 to 674 and tonnage from 545 to 744 tons year on year, with tonnage up about 32.84%. Management said it expects to close FY27 at ₹580–600 Cr revenue and targets roughly double the PAT margin, with H1 EBITDA cited as ₹12.5 Cr. Strategic items discussed were a proposed Dubai acquisition (NatWest), retail courier launch, ocean freight build-out, South America entry and a planned booking platform.

segments.name: Perishables (agro, fresh, temperature-controlled)
segments.commentary: About 45% of revenue; management calls it a niche, time-sensitive business where the company is the largest in India by volume, including mangoes to US and UK and roses.

segments.name: General cargo (incl. courier and e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Courier and e-commerce estimated at 25–30% of general cargo volumes; 98% of business is international per management.

segments.name: Ocean freight
segments.commentary: Small today (sea imports described as negligible); centralised in a Delhi team and targeted for growth in bulk and rice, with no revenue target given.

segments.name: Air import and sea import
segments.commentary: Described as negligible; management plans to build these over time.

guidance_outlook: Management aims to roughly double PAT margin from current levels; H1 EBITDA cited at ₹12.5 Cr.
Retail courier (B2C) launched in October 2026 after wholesale courier business; no revenue target given.
Tech platform (booking and rate engine for franchisees) expected to be ready by end-2026, per management.
Dubai acquisition (NatWest) not yet completed; management sees little contribution in FY27 and significant growth in FY28.
Management expects fuel-driven freight rate pressure to persist at least until end-2026.
capex_capacity: All warehouses are leased; the company owns no land or warehouses and operates an asset-light model with surface transport outsourced.
Current infrastructure can handle about double the present business volume, per management, so costs should stay flat as volumes rise.
Ocean freight team centralised in a large Delhi office; 8–9 major shipping lines are key carrier partners.
South America: a senior hire made in Brazil, with a back-office team in India; local operations are to follow in about a year if volumes build.
Dubai acquisition (NatWest) under way to take charter brokering and Gulf/Saudi business in-house.
demand_pricing: Management says it passes through freight cost changes and maintains margins; industry margins quoted at 10–25%, sometimes 7–8%.
Freight rate increases are route-specific (e.g., routing constraints and war-related), and fuel prices drive freight costs.
Growth partly from new e-commerce shops and end consumers, plus organic growth from existing customers; one customer's volume reportedly doubled.
Charter demand from Gulf supermarkets (e.g., Lulu, Nesto) rose, with about 70 charters since March, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How does the e-commerce and courier business operate, its domestic/international mix, revenue and EBITDA contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 98% of business is international, mainly wholesale consolidation to US, UK, Europe, Australia and NZ; retail B2B/B2C is starting. No revenue or EBITDA split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 96% air, perishable and general cargo mix intended to be maintained, or will ocean, courier and others grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Courier sits within general cargo. Management said ocean freight must be pursued for sheer scale, but it will be taken slowly.

qa_highlights.question: Dubai acquisition: business mix, geographic coverage, synergies, valuation, and financial impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The target (NatWest) covers UAE, Gulf and Saudi. Valuation was based on future orders from its promoters' linked customers. The deal is not complete, so no FY27 impact is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Ocean freight: capabilities, carrier partnerships and medium-term revenue target?
qa_highlights.answer: Ocean team is centralised in Delhi; relationships with about 8–9 major shipping lines. No medium-term revenue target was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 41% Q2 YoY revenue growth came from volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: No split was given. Management cited a sales process for volume growth and route-specific pricing, with fuel costs affecting freight rates.

qa_highlights.question: Courier shipments and tonnage decreased YoY; what is the driver?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed growth to new routes (direct flights to destinations like Germany), new e-commerce customers and organic growth at existing customers.

qa_highlights.question: Brazil/South America: current stage and milestones?
qa_highlights.answer: A senior person hired in Brazil; inquiries have turned into some business. Own operations are possible in about a year once volumes increase.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company own land, and will margins improve with volume?
qa_highlights.answer: No land is owned and all warehouses are leased. Management expects margins and bottom line to rise quarter on quarter as costs stay flat.

risks_watch: Revenue split between volume and price for the 41% Q2 YoY growth was not disclosed.
Dubai acquisition (NatWest) valuation rests on future orders and is incomplete; NatWest revenue reportedly below ₹1 Cr.
Fuel-linked freight rate volatility and geopolitical route disruption could affect margins.
Thin PAT margin of about 1.5% leaves little buffer against cost swings.
Courier volume decline YoY was raised by an analyst but only partly reconciled by management.
Retail courier and tech platform (end-2026) are unproven; ocean freight and South America remain early-stage.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth plans and margin outlook, but answers were often unstructured and gave few quantified targets (no ocean revenue target, no acquisition financials, no volume/price split).
key_quotes: Whatever our margins are, even if the Freight is double, tripled, we'll still maintain our margins.
Currently, we do not have any warehouses that are owned, everything is leased.
So, margin, bottom line, you will see increasing quarter on quarter and year on year, definitely.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue to ₹580–600 Cr, but the brief gives no implied growth rate and the backing is mostly volume momentum (tonnage up ~33% YoY in H1), a Dubai acquisition not yet closed, and a new B2C courier launch with no revenue target; infrastructure is leased and said to handle about double current volume, with no new capacity additions quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says it aims to roughly double the PAT margin from about 1.5% and expects margins to rise quarter on quarter as costs stay flat, but fuel-driven freight rate pressure is expected to persist at least until end-2026 and the H1 EBITDA margin is only 4.58%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: All warehouses are leased, no land or owned warehouses, and existing infrastructure is said to handle about double current volume, so no new physical capacity is quantified in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 tonnage rose about 32.84% (545 to 744 tons) and shipments about 56% (430 to 674), with ~70 Gulf charters since March and one customer's volume reportedly doubling, supporting the ₹580-600 Cr FY27 revenue guide.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Asset-light model with all warehouses leased and no capex discussed; infrastructure said to handle about double current volume, so utilisation pressure is not evident.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided to ₹580-600 Cr with H1 EBITDA at ₹12.5 Cr, but the brief gives no implied H2 run-rate and the 41% Q2 YoY growth was not split between volume and price.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Thin 1.5% PAT margin leaves little buffer, and fuel-linked freight rate pressure is expected to persist at least until end-2026; the courier volume decline YoY was only partly reconciled.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Retail B2C courier launched in October 2026 and a tech booking/rate platform is expected by end-2026, but neither has a revenue target and both are unproven.

rows.label: Dubai acquisition (NatWest) and South America entry
rows.why: Dubai deal is not complete with little FY27 contribution expected and NatWest revenue reportedly below ₹1 Cr; South America has a senior hire in Brazil with local operations possible in about a year if volumes build.

rows.label: Ocean freight build-out
rows.why: Ocean freight is small today, centralised in Delhi with 8-9 shipping lines, and targeted for bulk and rice growth, but no revenue target was given and it will be taken slowly.

rows.label: Fuel-driven route-specific freight rate pressure
rows.why: Management expects fuel-driven freight rate pressure to persist at least until end-2026, and says it passes through cost changes while industry margins run 7-25%.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 revenue of ₹580-600 Cr, margin doubling and new ventures, but was vague on the volume/price split, Dubai financials and ocean targets, while analysts pressed on the courier volume decline and the mix of the 41% Q2 growth.
